title: FIPS gate: wolfssl_fips_gate compares \!= FIPS_OPERATIONAL not \!= 0; correctness unverifiable in stub build
description: wolfssl_fips_gate() checks 'if (status \!= FIPS_OPERATIONAL)' where FIPS_OPERATIONAL is the wolfCrypt FIPS enum value from <wolfssl/wolfcrypt/fips.h>. wolfCrypt's own linuxkm/module_hooks.c checks 'if (ret \!= 0)' for the same wolfCrypt_GetStatus_fips() return value everywhere. The two idioms are only equivalent if wolfCrypt defines FIPS_OPERATIONAL == 0. In the current repo, wolfssl/wolfcrypt/fips.h is an empty stub (0 bytes), so FIPS_OPERATIONAL is undefined in non-FIPS builds; the gate is guarded by #if defined(HAVE_FIPS) so it compiles, but the assumption that FIPS_OPERATIONAL == 0 cannot be verified from the codebase. If a future wolfCrypt FIPS header defines FIPS_OPERATIONAL as a non-zero sentinel (e.g., an enum value), the gate would treat wolfCrypt's 0-return as non-operational and block all crypto. Consequence at audit or deployment: gate silently rejects all operations in a correctly-operational FIPS module. Fix: use 'if (status \!= 0)' to match wolfCrypt's own convention, and add a BUILD_BUG_ON or static_assert verifying FIPS_OPERATIONAL == 0 if the constant must be referenced.
